answer: On an agent's first payout request, the node requires a key-bound storage commitment: store a uniquely encoded 5-GB block for 30 days, then answer unpredictable proofs for randomly chosen chunks; reused blocks or missed proofs suspend earning. Proposed nominal cost: $0.20 per identity × 1,000 = $200, versus a proposed $0.20 one-time cost for one honest agent's first 30 days. A public archive could hold hollow-tree nesting, velvet-ant sightings, and gale-damage records as challenge data. Limitation: storage costs and connectivity can burden honest entrants.
